schema.description: Entra ID `userPrincipalName` (UPN), the user’s sign-in identifier. Required and unique across all users. This is NOT the user’s name. On create: if the request supplies a `userName`, use it as-is. Otherwise generate one from the full name (`givenName` + `familyName`): split into space-delimited tokens, join them with `.`, lowercase, and transliterate to plain ASCII (remove accents and expand ligatures: æ -> ae, ø -> o, å -> a, ä -> a, ö -> o, ü -> u, é -> e, è -> e, ñ -> n, ß -> ss). Then remove all characters except `a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `-` and `_`, collapse repeated periods and trim leading/trailing periods, limit the result to 64 characters, and append `@my-company.com`. Example: `Åse Kari Kjærøy` -> `ase.kari.kjaeroy@my-company.com`. On HTTP 409 Conflict: if creation fails with `HTTP 409 Conflict` because `userName` is already taken (SCIM `scimType: uniqueness`), insert a number directly before the `@` character, starting at 2, then retry. The domain `@my-company.com` must stay at the end. Example: `ase.kari.kjaeroy@my-company.com` -> `ase.kari.kjaeroy2@my-company.com`. WRONG: `ase.kari.kjaeroy@my-company.com2`. Try numbers 2-5, then report failure. On update: do not change `userName` unless explicitly requested.

Country where the user consumes Microsoft services, as ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (e.g. NO, US) or a supported country name. Required by Entra ID for license assignment: users without `usageLocation` cannot receive licenses (including via group-based licensing or access packages). On create: always set it. Use the stated `usageLocation`; otherwise derive it from the user's `country`; otherwise use `NO`. Not the same as `country` (postal address only). On modify: change only when explicitly requested; changing it can make licensed services unavailable.

map.comment1: map.user and map.group automatically generate schemas based on the default SCIM schemas. These defaults can be overridden by including a `schema` object containing standard schema attributes.
map.comment2: If using AI Agent and MCP tools, the `user.userPrincipalName.schema.description` must have the domain `@my-company.com` replaced with your actual domain or use `endpoint.entity.xxx.mapOverride.user.userPrincipalName.schema.description` to override for a specific baseEntity.
map.comment3: If using AI Agent and MCP tools, the `user.usageLocation.schema.description` defaults to `NO` and must be changed accordingly
map.comment4: user.signInActivity: requires Entra ID P1/P2 license and the API permissions: `AuditLog.Read.All`. Remove this mapping if conditions not met.
map.comment5: user.roles: managing eligible directory roles requires Entra ID P2 or Entra ID Governance (PIM) and the `RoleEligibilitySchedule.ReadWrite.Directory` API permission. Managing permanent role assignments requires the `RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory` API permission. Remove this mapping if the required permissions and licenses are not available.

Read-only Entra ID sign-in data (requires an Entra ID P1/P2 tenant). Use `lastSuccessfulSignInDateTime` to judge activity. If signInActivity is missing for a user while other users have it, the user has never signed in. If it is missing for all users, sign-in data is unavailable.

subAttributes.name: lastSignInDateTime
subAttributes.description: Last interactive sign-in attempt, successful or failed. Do not use for inactivity.

subAttributes.name: lastSuccessfulSignInDateTime
subAttributes.description: Last successful sign-in (interactive or non-interactive). The only reliable activity indicator.

subAttributes.name: lastNonInteractiveSignInDateTime
subAttributes.description: Last non-interactive sign-in attempt (a client signing in on the user’s behalf), successful or failed. Do not use for inactivity.

schema.description: Read-only attribute object (except for `mfa.reset`) presenting the user’s MFA capabilities. Note: `mfa.isMfaCapable` does not mean MFA is enabled for the user. Conditional Access policies or using Security Defaults must be verified separately.

subAttributes.name: isMfaCapable
subAttributes.description: true/false - user has at least one MFA-capable method registered (members only; for guests, methods are in home tenant and enforcement is via Conditional Access).

subAttributes.name: isLegacyEnabled
subAttributes.description: true/false - legacy per-user MFA is enabled (`perUserMfaState` is `enabled` or `enforced`); such users bypass/aren’t fully controlled by standard Conditional Access only design and therefore require special attention.

subAttributes.name: reset
subAttributes.description: Set to `true` will reset user’s MFA capabilities and user will be forced to re-register MFA. Only set when explicitly requested; confirm the target `userName` with the requester before sending.

schema.description: The user’s Entra ID directory role assignments with types `permanent` or `eligible`. Look up role ids with `list_roles`.
schema.roles.type.description: A tag used to categorize the user’s role, either `permanent` or `eligible`. Omit when adding (defaults to `eligible` if the tenant uses PIM; otherwise, defaults to `permanent`) unless the user specifies it; include when removing.
schema.roles.display.description: The role’s display name (the `displayName` from `list_roles`). Recommended when adding.

schema.description: The user’s entitlements with types `license` or `access-package` which is the Entra ID assigned Licenses and Access Packages. Look up ids with `list_entitlements`. Licenses are read-only; only Access Packages can be added or removed.
schema.entitlements.type.description: A tag used to categorize the user’s entitlement, either `license` (read-only) or `access-package`.
schema.entitlements.display.description: The entitlement’s display name (the `displayName` from `list_entitlements`). Recommended when adding.

schema.description: `Member` or `Guest`. On create: always `Member`.
The user’s administrative status: `true` means enabled and `false` means disabled. On create: `true` unless otherwise stated. On modify: `false` to disable, `true` to enable.
The given (first, including middle) name(s): all tokens of the full name except the last, unless the given name is stated explicitly.

parent-schema.description: The user’s real name and its components, including given and family names.

schema.description: The family (last) name: the final token of the full name, unless family name is stated explicitly.
The user’s full name (`givenName` + `familyName`). On create: if not supplied, use `givenName` + space + `familyName`.
The user’s job title.
The user’s identifier assigned by the organization.
The user’s employee type (e.g., `Contractor`, `Intern`, `Permanent`, `Temp`).
The user’s hire date. Date format must be YYYY-MM-DD.
The user’s company name.
The user’s cost center name.

parent-schema.description: The user’s organization information like cost center and division.

schema.description: The user’s division name.
The user’s office location.
The user’s department name.
The manager’s `id` attribute. Never a `userName` or `displayName`. Set to "" to clear the manager.

parent-schema.description: The user’s manager, referenced by the manager’s `id` attribute in `manager.managerId`

schema.description: The user’s email address. On Create: Set equal to the final `userName` (including any number added on conflict)
The user’s casual name. On Create: Set equal to the final `userName` and omitting the `@domain` suffix.

The user’s proxy addresses. Important: This field is read-only during user creation. The agent MUST NOT include this field in the initial create user request. To set proxy addresses, first create the user, then use a separate modify user request to add them.
The user’s mobile phone number.
The user’s work phone number. Entra ID accepts only one value.
The user’s fax number.
The user’s country.
The user’s city.
The user’s street address.
The user’s postal code.
The user’s state.
Read-only attribute representing Entra ID password policies.
Force user to change password on next sign-in. On create and on password change: set to `true` unless explicitly specified otherwise by the user.

parent-schema.description: The user’s password profile. On create, set `password` (generated) and `forceChangePasswordNextSignIn`. On modify, send both when changing the password.

schema.description: The user’s clear-text password, used to set an initial password or reset it. On create: the agent MUST generate a secure random password using ASCII-only characters and following `x-agent-schema`; Entra ID may reject non-ASCII characters. Do not derive it from the user’s name or personal data, and do not prompt the user for this password. On reset: if the user supplies a password, set it as given without asking for confirmation; otherwise generate one as on create. When a password is generated, show it once to the requester so it can be handed over.

Country where the user consumes Microsoft services, as ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (e.g. NO, US) or a supported country name. Required by Entra ID for license assignment: users without `usageLocation` cannot receive licenses (including via group-based licensing or access packages). On create: always set it. Use the stated `usageLocation`; otherwise derive it from the user's `country`; otherwise use `NO`. Not the same as `country` (postal address only). On modify: change only when explicitly requested; changing it can make licensed services unavailable.
The user’s preferred language. A two-letter lowercase ISO 639 language code, a hyphen, then a two-letter uppercase ISO 3166 country/region code like `nb-NO`.
Read-only attribute representing the user’s Entra ID `onPremisesSyncEnabled`. When `true` this user is synchronized from an on-premises Active Directory and can not be modified or deleted.
Read-only attribute representing the user’s Entra ID `onPremisesImmutableId`.
A human-readable description of the group.
`true` or `false`, `true` represents an Entra ID security group. On Create: The agent MUST always set this value to `true`. IMPORTANT: This field is read-only after the group is created.
`true` or `false`, `true` represents an Entra ID mail enabled group. On Create: The agent MUST always set this value to `false`. IMPORTANT: This field is read-only after the group is created.
